2:  * BK7258 mailbox v2 logical channels used by AP bring-up and logging.
3:  ****************************************************************************/

17: #include "hardware/bk7258_mbox.h"
18: 
19: #define MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL_TX 0x10u
20: #define MB_CHNL_PWC_TX     0x12u
21: #define MB_CHNL_UART0_TX   0x19u
22: #define MB_CHNL_PWC_RX     0x42u
23: #define MB_CHNL_UART0_RX   0x49u
24: 
25: #define MB_UART_SEND_DATA  0u
26: #define MB_UART_SEND_STATE 1u
27: 
28: #define CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX  0x01u
29: #define CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX  0x02u
30: #define CHNL_CTRL_RESET    0x04u
31: #define CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL 0x01u
32: 
33: #define CP_RAM_START       0x28064000u
34: #define CP_RAM_END         0x2809f700u
35: #define UART_XCHG_SIZE     128u
36: #ifndef CONFIG_BK7258_MBOX_LOG_BUFSIZE
37: #  define CONFIG_BK7258_MBOX_LOG_BUFSIZE 8192u
38: #endif
39: #define UART_TX_SIZE       CONFIG_BK7258_MBOX_LOG_BUFSIZE
40: #define PHY_BUSY_TIMEOUT   MSEC2TICK(200)
41: #define TX_RETRY_INTERVAL  MSEC2TICK(10)
42: 
43: struct mb_message
44: {
45:   uint32_t header;
46:   uint32_t param1;
47:   uint32_t param2;
48:   uint32_t param3;
49: };
50: 
51: struct logical_channel
52: {
53:   struct mb_message message __attribute__((aligned(32)));
54:   bool pending;
55: };
56: 
57: struct mailbox_stats
58: {
59:   uint32_t tx_count;
60:   uint32_t rx_count;
61:   uint32_t fifo_full;
62:   uint32_t ack_timeout;
63:   uint32_t bad_envelope;
64:   uint32_t bad_ack;
65:   uint32_t reset_count;
66:   uint32_t uart_drop;
67:   uint32_t uart_drop_events;
68:   uint32_t uart_tx_fail;
69:   uint32_t uart_write_calls;
70:   uint32_t uart_write_bytes;
71: };
72: 
73: static struct logical_channel g_channels[3];
74: static const uint8_t g_channel_ids[3] =
75: {
76:   MB_CHNL_PWC_TX,
77:   MB_CHNL_HW_CTRL_TX,
78:   MB_CHNL_UART0_TX
79: };
80: static uint8_t g_uart_tx[UART_TX_SIZE];
81: static uint8_t g_uart_xchg[UART_XCHG_SIZE] __attribute__((aligned(32)));
82: static struct mb_message g_ack_message __attribute__((aligned(32)));
83: static uint32_t g_ack_wire[2];
84: static uint16_t g_uart_read;
85: static uint16_t g_uart_write;
86: static uint16_t g_uart_inflight;
87: static uint8_t g_tx_seq;
88: static uint8_t g_active_channel;
89: static uint8_t g_active_seq;
90: static bool g_phy_busy;
91: static bool g_initialized;
92: static bool g_serial_kick;
93: static clock_t g_busy_since;
94: static clock_t g_uart_retry_after;
95: static struct mailbox_stats g_stats;
96: static sem_t g_tx_sem;
97: static void (*g_pwc_rx)(const struct mb_message *message);
98: 
99: void bk7258_mbox_uart_early_init(void)
100: {
101:   /* The BSS-backed ring is intentionally available before Mailbox init. */
102: }
103: 
104: extern void bk7258_serial_tx_available(void);
105: 
106: static unsigned int channel_index(uint8_t logical_channel)
107: {
108:   unsigned int i;
109: 
110:   for (i = 0; i < sizeof(g_channel_ids); i++)
111:     {
112:       if (g_channel_ids[i] == logical_channel)
113:         {
114:           return i;
115:         }
116:     }
117: 
118:   return sizeof(g_channel_ids);
119: }
120: 
121: static uint16_t uart_count(void)
122: {
123:   if (g_uart_write >= g_uart_read)
124:     {
125:       return g_uart_write - g_uart_read;
126:     }
127: 
128:   return UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart_read + g_uart_write;
129: }
130: 
131: static void uart_prepare(void)
132: {
133:   struct logical_channel *channel = &g_channels[2];
134:   uint16_t count;
135:   uint16_t first;
136: 
137:   if (channel->pending || g_uart_inflight != 0)
138:     {
139:       return;
140:     }
141: 
142:   if ((int32_t)(clock_systime_ticks() - g_uart_retry_after) < 0)
143:     {
144:       return;
145:     }
146: 
147:   count = uart_count();
148:   if (count == 0)
149:     {
150:       return;
151:     }
152: 
153:   if (count > UART_XCHG_SIZE)
154:     {
155:       count = UART_XCHG_SIZE;
156:     }
157: 
158:   first = UART_TX_SIZE - g_uart_read;
159:   if (first > count)
160:     {
161:       first = count;
162:     }
163: 
164:   memcpy(g_uart_xchg, &g_uart_tx[g_uart_read], first);
165:   if (first != count)
166:     {
167:       memcpy(&g_uart_xchg[first], g_uart_tx, count - first);
168:     }
169: 
170:   channel->message.header = 0; /* MB_UART_SEND_DATA */
171:   channel->message.param1 = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)g_uart_xchg;
172:   channel->message.param2 = count;
173:   channel->message.param3 = 0; /* RTS deasserted, CRC disabled by Armino. */
174:   channel->pending = true;
175:   g_uart_inflight = count;
176: }
177: 
178: static int dispatch_locked(void)
179: {
180:   struct logical_channel *channel;
181:   uint32_t wire[2];

389: static void mailbox_rx(const bk7258_mbox_message_t *wire)
390: {
391:   struct mb_message message;
392:   uintptr_t address;
393:   uint8_t control;
394:   uint8_t logical_channel;
395:   irqstate_t flags;

397:   if (!valid_cp_message(wire, &address))

399:       g_stats.bad_envelope++;
400:       return;
401:     }
402: 
403:   memcpy(&message, (const void *)address, sizeof(message));
404:   control = (message.header >> 12) & 0x0fu;
405:   logical_channel = message.header >> 24;
406:   g_stats.rx_count++;
407: 
408:   flags = up_irq_save();
409:   if ((control & CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX) != 0)
410:     {
411:       handle_ack(&message);
412:       up_irq_restore(flags);
413:       return;
414:     }
415: 
416:   if (logical_channel != MB_CHNL_PWC_RX &&
417:       logical_channel != MB_CHNL_UART0_RX)
418:     {
419:       g_stats.bad_envelope++;
420:       up_irq_restore(flags);
421:       return;
422:     }
423: 
424:   if (logical_channel == MB_CHNL_UART0_RX)
425:     {
426:       /* This port is output-only, but Armino initializes MB_UART0 by sending
427:        * SEND_STATE from CP. Acknowledge its state/data commands with RTS
428:        * deasserted so the CP endpoint reaches ready without enabling input. */

430:           (message.header & 0xffu) != MB_UART_SEND_STATE)

432:           message.header |= (uint32_t)CHNL_STATE_COM_FAIL << 8;
433:         }
434: 
435:       message.param1 = 0; /* uart_rts=0, uart_tx_fail=0 */
436:       message.param2 = 0;
437:       message.param3 = 0;
438:     }
439: 
440:   if ((control & CHNL_CTRL_SYNC_TX) == 0)
441:     {
442:       message.header |= (uint32_t)CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX << 12;
443:       memcpy((void *)address, &message, sizeof(message));
444:       memcpy(&g_ack_message, &message, sizeof(g_ack_message));
445:       g_ack_wire[0] = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)&g_ack_message;
446:       g_ack_wire[1] = sizeof(g_ack_message);
447:       __asm__ volatile("dmb sy" ::: "memory");
448:       if (bk7258_mbox_send(0, g_ack_wire) < 0)
449:         {
450:           g_stats.fifo_full++;
451:           nxsem_post(&g_tx_sem);
452:         }
453:       else
454:         {
455:           g_ack_wire[0] = 0;
456:           g_stats.tx_count++;
457:         }
458: 
459:       message.header &= ~((uint32_t)CHNL_CTRL_ACK_BOX << 12);
460:     }
461: 
462:   if (logical_channel == MB_CHNL_PWC_RX && g_pwc_rx != NULL)
463:     {
464:       g_pwc_rx(&message);
465:     }
466: 
467:   up_irq_restore(flags);
468: }

56: static void pwc_rx(const void *raw)
57: {
58:   const uint8_t *bytes = raw;
59:   struct pwc_message message;
60:   unsigned int next = (g_head + 1u) % PM_QUEUE_DEPTH;
61:   if (next == g_tail || bytes == NULL)
62:     {

64:     }
65:   message.header = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[0];
66:   message.param1 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[1];
67:   message.param2 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[2];
68:   message.param3 = ((const uint32_t *)bytes)[3];
69:   g_queue[g_head] = message;
70:   g_head = next;

56: /* Configuration ************************************************************/
57: 
58: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_HIPRI_INTERRUPT
59:   /* In protected mode without an interrupt stack, this interrupt handler will set the
60:    * MSP to the stack pointer of the interrupted thread.  If the interrupted thread
61:    * was a privileged thread, that will be the MSP otherwise it will be the PSP.  If
62:    * the PSP is used, then the value of the MSP will be invalid when the interrupt
63:    * handler returns because it will be a pointer to an old position in the
64:    * unprivileged stack.  Then when the high priority interrupt occurs and uses this
65:    * stale MSP, there will most likely be a system failure.
66:    *
67:    * If the interrupt stack is selected, on the other hand, then the interrupt
68:    * handler will always set the MSP to the interrupt stack.  So when the high
69:    * priority interrupt occurs, it will either use the MSP of the last privileged
70:    * thread to run or, in the case of the nested interrupt, the interrupt stack if
71:    * no privileged task has run.
72:    */
73: 
74: #  if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_PROTECTED) && CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK < 8
75: #    error Interrupt stack must be used with high priority interrupts in protected mode
76: #  endif
77: #endif

96: /* Common exception handling logic.  On entry here, the return stack is on either
97:  * the PSP or the MSP and looks like the following:
98:  *
99:  *      REG_XPSR
100:  *      REG_R15
101:  *      REG_R14
102:  *      REG_R12
103:  *      REG_R3
104:  *      REG_R2
105:  *      REG_R1
106:  * MSP->REG_R0
107:  *
108:  * And
109:  *      IPSR contains the IRQ number
110:  *      R14 Contains the EXC_RETURN value
111:  *      We are in handler mode and the current SP is the MSP
112:  *
113:  * If CONFIG_ARCH_FPU is defined, the volatile FP registers and FPSCR are on the
114:  * return stack immediately above REG_XPSR.
115:  */
116: 
117: 	.text
118: 	.align 2
119: 	.section    .text.exception_common, "ax"
120: #ifdef __ghs__
121: 	.type	exception_common, $function
122: #else
123: 	.thumb_func
124: 	.syntax	unified
125: 	.type	exception_common, function
126: #endif

132: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE

134: #endif

136: 
137: 	/* The EXC_RETURN value tells us whether the context is on the MSP or PSP */
138: 
139: 	mov		r0, r14					/* Copy EXC_RETURN */

142: 	mrs		r1, psp					/* R1=The process stack pointer (PSP) */
143: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
144: 	mrs		r0, psplim
145: 	msr		psplim, r3
146: #endif
147: 	b		2f
148: 1:
149: 	mrs		r1, msp					/* R1=The main stack pointer (MSP) */
150: 	mov		r0, r1					/* Keep r1 not changed for push */
151: 	subs		r0, #SW_XCPT_SIZE			/* Reserve MSP for SW_XCPT_SIZE */
152: 	msr		msp, r0					/* Reserved stack space */
153: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
154: 	mrs		r0, msplim
155: 	msr		msplim, r3
156: #endif
157: 	isb		sy
158: 2:
159: 	mov		r2, r1					/* R2=Copy of the main/process stack pointer */
160: 	adds		r2, #HW_XCPT_SIZE			/* R2=MSP/PSP before the interrupt was taken */
161: 								/* (ignoring the xPSR[9] alignment bit) */
162: #ifdef CONFIG_ARMV8M_STACKCHECK_HARDWARE
163: 	stmdb		r1!, {r0, r3}
164: #endif
165: 
166: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
167: 	mrs		r3, primask				/* R3=Current PRIMASK setting */
168: #else
169: 	mrs		r3, basepri				/* R3=Current BASEPRI setting */
170: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M */
171: 
172: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_FPU
173: 
174: 	/* Save the non-volatile FP registers here.
175: 	 *
176: 	 * This routine is the only point where we can save these registers; either before
177: 	 * or after calling arm_doirq.  The compiler is free to use them at any time as long
178: 	 * as they are restored before returning, so we can't assume that we can get at the
179: 	 * true values of these registers in any routine called from here.
180: 	 *
181: 	 * REVISIT: we could do all this saving lazily on the context switch side if we knew
182: 	 * where to put the registers.
183: 	 */
184: 
185: 	/* Switched-out task including volatile FP registers ? */
186: 
187: 	tst		r14, #EXC_RETURN_STD_CONTEXT
188: 	ite		eq
189: 	vstmdbeq	r1!, {s16-s31}			/* Save the non-volatile FP context */
190: 	subne		r1, #(4*SW_FPU_REGS)
191: 
192: 	/* the FPSCR[18:16] LTPSIZE field must be set to 0b100 for
193: 	 * "Tail predication not applied" as it's reset value.
194: 	 */
195: 
196: 	mov		r0, #ARM_FPSCR_LTPSIZE_NONE

198: #endif
199: 
200: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M
201: 	subs		r1, #(4*SW_INT_REGS)		/* Move cursor to base, for save low regs first */
202: 	mov		r0, r1				/* Copy the context array pointer */
203: 	stmia		r0!, {r2-r7}			/* Save the SP, PRIMASK, and R4-R7 in the context array */
204: 
205: 	/* Save R8-R11 control and the EXEC_RETURN value in the context array */
206: 
207: 	mov		r2, r8				/* Copy high registers to low */
208: 	mov		r3, r9
209: 	mov		r4, r10
210: 	mov		r5, r11
211: 	mrs		r6, control			/* R6=control */
212: 	mov		r7, r14
213: 	stmia		r0!, {r2-r7}			/* Save the high registers r8-r11 control and r14 */
214: #else
215: 	stmdb		r1!, {r2-r12,r14}		/* Save the remaining registers plus the SP/PRIMASK values */
216: #endif /* CONFIG_ARCH_ARMV6M */

218: 	/* There are two arguments to arm_doirq:
219: 	 *

244: 	lsls		r2, #(31 - EXC_RETURN_THREAD_BITNO)	/* Move to bit 31 */

74: /* This is an array of task control block (TCB) for the IDLE thread of each
75:  * CPU.  For the non-SMP case, this is a a single TCB; For the SMP case,
76:  * there is one TCB per CPU.  NOTE: The system boots on CPU0 into the IDLE
77:  * task.  The IDLE task later starts the other CPUs and spawns the user
78:  * initialization task.  That user initialization task is responsible for
79:  * bringing up the rest of the system.
80:  */
81: 
82: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS(struct tcb_s, g_idletcb);
83: 
84: /* Task Lists ***************************************************************/
85: 
86: /* The state of a task is indicated both by the task_state field of the TCB
87:  * and by a series of task lists.  All of these tasks lists are declared
88:  * below. Although it is not always necessary, most of these lists are
89:  * prioritized so that common list handling logic can be used (only the
90:  * g_readytorun, the g_pendingtasks, and the g_waitingforsemaphore lists
91:  * need to be prioritized).
92:  */
93: 
94: /* This is the list of all tasks that are ready to run.  This is a
95:  * prioritized list with head of the list holding the highest priority
96:  * (unassigned) task.  In the non-SMP case, the head of this list is the
97:  * currently active task and the tail of this list, the lowest priority
98:  * task, is always the IDLE task.
99:  */
100: 
101: #undef g_readytorun
102: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BMP(dq_queue_t, g_readytorun) =
103: {
104: #if !defined(CONFIG_SMP)
105:   (FAR dq_entry_t *)&per_cpu_var_smp(g_idletcb, 0),
106:   (FAR dq_entry_t *)&per_cpu_var_smp(g_idletcb, 0),
107: #endif
108: };
109: #define g_readytorun this_cpu_var_bmp(g_readytorun)
110: 
111: /* In order to support SMP, the function of the g_readytorun list changes,
112:  * The g_readytorun is still used but in the SMP case it will contain only:
113:  *
114:  *  - Only tasks/threads that are eligible to run, but not currently running,
115:  *    and
116:  *  - Tasks/threads that have not been assigned to a CPU.
117:  *
118:  * Otherwise, the running TCB will be retained in g_assignedtasks vector.
119:  * As its name suggests, on 'g_assignedtasks vector for CPU
120:  * 'n' would contain the task/thread which is assigned to CPU 'n'.  Tasks/
121:  * threads would be assigned a particular CPU by one of two mechanisms:
122:  *
123:  *  - (Semi-)permanently through an RTOS interfaces such as
124:  *    pthread_attr_setaffinity(), or
125:  *  - Temporarily through scheduling logic when a previously unassigned task
126:  *    is made to run.
127:  */
128: 
129: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
130: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS_SMP(struct tcb_s *, g_assignedtasks);
131: 
132: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS_SMP(enum task_deliver_e, g_delivertasks);
133: #endif
134: 
135: /* g_running_tasks[] holds a references to the running task for each CPU.
136:  * It is valid only when up_interrupt_context() returns true.
137:  */
138: 
139: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS(FAR struct tcb_s *, g_running_tasks);
140: 
141: /* This is the list of all tasks that are ready-to-run, but cannot be placed
142:  * in the g_readytorun list because:  (1) They are higher priority than the
143:  * currently active task at the head of the g_readytorun list, and (2) the
144:  * currently active task has disabled pre-emption.
145:  */

147: #ifndef CONFIG_SMP
148: #  undef g_pendingtasks
149: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS_BMP(dq_queue_t, g_pendingtasks);
150: #  define g_pendingtasks this_cpu_var_bmp(g_pendingtasks)
151: #endif
152: 
153: /* This is the list of all tasks that are blocked waiting for a signal */

155: #undef g_waitingforsignal
156: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS_BMP(dq_queue_t, g_waitingforsignal);

165: #endif
166: 
167: #ifdef CONFIG_SIG_SIGSTOP_ACTION

169:  * via SIGSTOP or SIGTSTP
170:  */

173: #define g_stoppedtasks this_cpu_var_bmp(g_stoppedtasks)
174: #endif
175: 
176: /* This list of all tasks that have been initialized, but not yet
177:  * activated. NOTE:  This is the only list that is not prioritized.
178:  */

180: #undef g_inactivetasks
181: DEFINE_PER_CPU_BSS_BMP(dq_queue_t, g_inactivetasks);
182: #define g_inactivetasks this_cpu_var_bmp(g_inactivetasks)
183:

188: #define g_lastpid this_cpu_var_bmp(g_lastpid)

190: /* The following hash table is used for two things:

207: #define g_pidhashlock this_cpu_var_bmp(g_pidhashlock)

209: /* This is a table of task lists.  This table is indexed by the task state
210:  * enumeration type (tstate_t) and provides a pointer to the associated
211:  * static task list (if there is one) as well as a set of attribute flags
212:  * indicating properties of the list, for example, if the list is an
213:  * ordered list or not.

269:

271:   tlist[TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN].attr = TLIST_ATTR_PRIORITIZED |
272:                                        TLIST_ATTR_RUNNABLE;
273: 
274:   /* TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING */
275: 
276:   tlist[TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING].list = list_readytorun();
277:   tlist[TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING].attr = TLIST_ATTR_PRIORITIZED |

279: #endif

283:   tlist[TSTATE_TASK_INACTIVE].list = list_inactivetasks();

286:   /* TSTATE_WAIT_SEM */

288:   tlist[TSTATE_WAIT_SEM].list = (FAR dq_queue_t *)offsetof(sem_t, waitlist);
289:   tlist[TSTATE_WAIT_SEM].attr = TLIST_ATTR_PRIORITIZED |
290:                                 TLIST_ATTR_OFFSET;

293: 
294:   tlist[TSTATE_WAIT_SIG].list = list_waitingforsignal();

text:
**审计结论**

本次只读审计以最终产物 [nuttx](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx)、[System.map](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/System.map:974)、[nuttx.map](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.map:2769)、[.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:189) 为准，并与适配源码交叉验证。ELF SHA-256 为 `96fe9af78244c305b3603a65bab302f90f82f1cc39acddae4c3ac0d3a62bc89c`。

**准确内存布局**

| 区域 | 地址范围 | 大小 | 实际情况 |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| AP FLASH | `0x02150000..0x02167ddf` | `0x17de0` = 97,760 B | 含 boot vectors、text/rodata、exidx |
| AP FLASH 预留 | `0x02150000..0x0225ffff` | `0x110000` = 1,114,112 B | 链接脚本上限 |
| AP SRAM | `0x28010000..0x28063fff` | `0x54000` = 344,064 B = 336 KiB | 唯一 allocator region |
| CP RAM 白名单 | `0x28064000..0x2809f6ff` | `0x3b700` = 243,456 B | 只用于校验 mailbox 入站指针 |
| heap | `0x28014a40..0x28063fff` | `0x4f5c0` = 325,056 B = 317.438 KiB | 单一 NuttX heap |

地址来源在 [ld.script](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/scripts/ld.script:7) 和 [bk7258_memorymap.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/hardware/bk7258_memorymap.h:12)。最终展开脚本完全一致，见 [ld.script.tmp](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/ld.script.tmp:4)。

**SRAM 实际使用**

ELF section 实测：

| section | 地址 | 大小 |
|---|---:|---:|
| `.data` | `0x28010000` | `0x364` = 868 B |
| 对齐空洞 | `0x28010364..0x280103ff` | 156 B |
| `.ram_vectors` | `0x28010400` | `0x140` = 320 B |
| `.bss` | `0x28010540` | `0x34fd` = 13,565 B |
| 对齐空洞 | `0x28013a3d..0x28013a3f` | 3 B |
| `.idle_stack` | `0x28013a40` | `0x1000` = 4,096 B |

因此：

- section 内容合计：`18,849 B`
- 含对齐空洞的链接时静态 SRAM span：`0x4a40 = 19,008 B = 18.5625 KiB`
- 链接后剩余、交给 heap：`325,056 B = 317.438 KiB`
- 静态占 SRAM：`5.525%`
- heap 占 SRAM：`94.475%`

关键最终符号见 [System.map](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/System.map:980)：`_sdata=0x28010000`、`_edata=0x28010364`、`_sbss=0x28010540`、`_ebss=0x28013a3d`、`__heap_start=0x28014a40`、`__heap_end=0x28064000`。

注意：`317.438 KiB` 是 heap 初始容量，不是系统启动完成后的实时 free heap。没有运行时 `mallinfo`/`/proc/meminfo` 快照，不能严谨声称启动后的精确空闲量。

**Heap 与运行时占用**

[up_allocate_heap()](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_allocateheap.c:18) 原样返回链接符号区间；`.config` 配置 `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=1`，见 [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:971)。没有第二 heap、kernel heap 或 task heap。

启动时可确定的持久线程栈至少为：

- `mbox-tx`：1,536 B，[bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:497)
- `ipc-heartbeat`：1,536 B，[bk7258_pm_pwc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:122)
- `pwc`：2,048 B，同文件第 127 行
- `power-key-motor`：1,536 B，[bk7258_motor.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_motor.c:135)
- `nsh_main` init：4,096 B，由 [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:412) 决定

持久栈申请总额至少 `10,752 B`；启动期间还会暂时存在 4,096 B `AppBringUp` 栈，见 [nx_bringup.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/sched/init/nx_bringup.c:450)。所以仅按已知栈扣除，稳定态 heap 理论上限约 `314,304 B`，启动重叠峰值约 `310,208 B`；TCB、task group、PID hash、文件结构和 allocator 元数据还会继续消耗，实际空闲必然更少。

**Mailbox buffers**

最终静态地址已经核实：

- UART 驱动 TX/RX：`0x28010540`/`0x28010640`，各 256 B
- mailbox stats：`0x28010758`，48 B
- ACK wire：`0x2801079c`，8 B
- ACK message：`0x280107c0`，16 B，32-byte 对齐
- exchange buffer：`0x280107e0`，128 B，32-byte 对齐
- log ring：`0x28010860`，`0x2000` = 8,192 B
- logical channels：`0x28012860`，96 B

对应源码见 [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:73)，配置来源为 [Kconfig](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/Kconfig:22) 和 [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:231)。

主要风险：CP 入站地址只做范围、长度和 4-byte 对齐校验，见 [bk7258_mailbox_channel.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:316)。CP RAM 不在 AP 显式 MPU RAM region 内，访问依赖 privileged default map，且入站 `memcpy` 前后没有 cache invalidate。若 CP RAM alias 可缓存或存在非一致 cache，会产生陈旧消息/ACK 风险。

**MPU**

启用了 MPU、8 regions、启动 reset，见 [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:189)。实际只使用 3 个 region，定义见 [bk7258_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:35)：

- FLASH `0x02150000 + 0x110000`：RO、可执行、write-through
- AP RAM `0x28010000 + 0x54000`：RW、XN、inner-shareable、non-cacheable
- `0x40000000 + 0x20000000`：RW、XN、device

风险：

- `mpu_initialize(..., false, true)` 打开 `PRIVDEFENA`，见 [bk7258_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:110)。privileged 代码可通过背景映射访问未配置区域，MPU 不是严格边界。
- 外设 region 整体 `0x40000000..0x5fffffff` 可 RW，范围非常宽。
- FLASH 和 RAM 权限宏均允许 user access；当前是 flat build，隔离价值有限。
- RAM 设为 non-cacheable，有利于 AP 发往 CP 的共享 mailbox buffer，但有性能代价。
- 5 个 MPU region 空闲，未用于 stack guard、heap guard 或 CP RAM 精细属性。

**SAU：最高风险**

SAU 编程见 [bk7258_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:73)：

- region 0：`0x00000000..0x0fffffff`，RLAR=`0x0fffffe3`
- region 1：`0x10000000..0xefffffff`，RLAR=`0xefffffe1`

RLAR bit 1 是 `NSC`，定义见 [sau.h](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/nuttx/arch/arm/src/arm_m/sau.h:78)。所以 region 0 被标记成超大 NSC 区，包含 AP FLASH `0x02150000`；region 1 是普通 Non-secure，并数值上包含 AP RAM `0x28010000` 和 CP RAM。

这与源码注释“secure alias retained”明显矛盾，是本审计最高严重度问题。除非 BK7258 在 SAU 之前还有厂商专用地址重映射/IDAU 覆盖，否则 secure AP 的代码与数据属性不符合常规 TrustZone 设计：NSC 应只覆盖很小的 SG veneer 区，而不应覆盖约 256 MiB；AP RAM 也不应落入普通 Non-secure region。最终 ELF `.gnu.sgstubs` 为空，进一步说明并没有与巨大 NSC 区匹配的 CMSE gateway。

**PSRAM**

结论是：本 AP NuttX 镜像没有启用或使用 PSRAM。

- `.config` 无 PSRAM/SPIRAM/EXTMEM 配置。
- 链接脚本没有 PSRAM MEMORY region 或 section。
- ELF 中没有 PSRAM 地址 section/symbol。
- `CONFIG_MM_REGIONS=1`，`arm_addregion()` 不生效且实现为空。
- MPU 没有 PSRAM region。
- 唯一相关代码只是被动接收 PWC 命令 `0x7`，并注明 PHY transition 由 CP 持有，见 [bk7258_pm_pwc.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:89)。

因此 PSRAM 容量为 allocator 可用 `0 B`。风险是所有任务栈、动态对象和应用数据都竞争 317.438 KiB 初始 SRAM heap；即便 CP 已给 PSRAM 上电，AP 当前也不能分配或链接到它。

**栈风险**

`CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK=2048` 存在于 [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:289)，但最终链接把 `arm_exception.S.o` 的 `0x800` 输入 `.bss` 丢弃了，见 [nuttx.map](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/nuttx.map:867)。最终 ELF 没有 `g_intstackalloc/g_intstacktop` 和独立 interrupt-stack section。

实际 MSP 从 `__idle_stack_top=0x28014a40` 启动，MSPLIM 设为 `0x28013a40`，见 [bk7258_start.c](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_start.c:128)。因此有效异常/MSP 空间是链接脚本预留的 4 KiB，而不是配置所暗示的独立 2 KiB interrupt stack。

同时 `.config` 关闭 stack coloration、canary、usage tracking 和 ARMv8-M hardware stack checking，见 [.config](/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:68)。除 MSP 的手工 MSPLIM 外，普通线程栈没有审计可见的溢出保护。这是高风险配置，尤其是多个 1.5 KiB worker 使用 mailbox、信号、信号量和 syslog 调用链时。
